title: Guidance: policy statements and interpretive rules
shortTitle: Guidance: policy statements and interpretive rules
summary: Guidance includes statements of enforcement policy and explanations of existing law; whether notice and comment is required depends on the statement’s legal character and operation.
notes:
APA § 553(b)(A) excepts interpretive rules and general policy statements from ordinary notice and comment. Guidance communicates an agency’s interpretation or intended exercise of discretion and can help field personnel and regulated people predict the agency’s position. Publication and disclosure obligations can still apply; exemption from notice and comment does not mean an agency may keep adopted guidance secret.

Pacific Gas describes a policy statement as a tentative announcement whose underlying policy remains open to challenge when applied. Community Nutrition complicates that account: an FDA action level could function as a binding norm by limiting the agency’s own enforcement discretion, even though the agency would still need to prove adulteration in court. Mandatory language, exemptions from an announced norm, and actual practice can reveal binding effect. Regulatory beneficiaries may be harmed by a safe harbor and have no later enforcement proceeding in which to contest it.

The distinction for interpretive rules is related but different. Such a rule explains an existing statute or legislative rule; the inquiry asks whether that existing law supplies the duty or whether the agency is exercising delegated lawmaking power to add one. The materials caution that the tests remain contested and cannot be reduced to a document’s label.
